items.title: Corporate Training in Brazilian Software Engineering: A Quantitative Study of Professional Perceptions
items.abstract: Context: Strategic corporate training is essential for the sustained professional development of software engineers. However, there is a knowledge gap regarding the factors that drive quality and effectiveness of such training from the professionals' perspective, and no validated instrument exists for assessing these factors in the software engineering (SE) domain. Objective: This study aims to quantitatively analyze which factors influence SE professionals' perceptions of corporate training quality and effectiveness. Method: A quantitative survey was conducted with 282 Brazilian SE professionals. A structured questionnaire was developed and polychoric correlation was adopted for data analysis. Results: Three tightly correlated factors (cognitive engagement, variety of activities, and instructor performance) emerged as the strongest predictors of perceived training quality and effectiveness. Mandatory participation significantly reduces motivation and perceived training quality. Perceived impact on personal time proved to be largely independent of training quality. These findings are consistent with the general training effectiveness literature. Conclusions: Training effectiveness in the SE context is predominantly determined by three factors: cognitive engagement, variety of activities, and instructor performance. Mandatory participation negatively influences motivation, perceived relevance, and perceived training quality, while also amplifying the perception of time burden. The consistency with the general literature suggests that software organizations do not need to reinvent training design principles and can apply established guidelines with confidence. Salas and Cannon-Bowers' framework produced coherent results in the SE context, making it a promising candidate for future psychometric validation.

items.title: Designing Digital Humans with Ambient Intelligence
items.abstract: Digital humans are lifelike virtual agents capable of natural conversation and are increasingly deployed in domains like retail and finance. However, most current digital humans operate in isolation from their surroundings and lack contextual awareness beyond the dialogue itself. We address this limitation by integrating ambient intelligence (AmI) - i.e., environmental sensors, IoT data, and contextual modeling - with digital human systems. This integration enables situational awareness of the user's environment, anticipatory and proactive assistance, seamless cross-device interactions, and personalized long-term user support. We present a conceptual framework defining key roles that AmI can play in shaping digital human behavior, a design space highlighting dimensions such as proactivity levels and privacy strategies, and application-driven patterns with case studies in financial and retail services. We also discuss an architecture for ambient-enabled digital humans and provide guidelines for responsible design regarding privacy and data governance. Together, our work positions ambient intelligent digital humans as a new class of interactive agents powered by AI that respond not only to users' queries but also to the context and situations in which the interaction occurs.

items.title: Gamification and Virtual Reality in Stroke and Vestibular Rehabilitation
items.abstract: Stroke and other disorders resulting in vestibular dysfunction are a leading cause of balance impairment and functional disability in adults, both in the United States and worldwide. In the United States, roughly 795,000 people a year experience a stroke, the majority of which are 65 and older (Martin et al., 2025). In that demographic, stroke reduces mobility in more than half of survivors, and much of this mobility loss attributable to balance deficits (Feigin et al., 2025). Globally, there are roughly 93.8 million patients who have suffered a stroke, with an annual global incidence rate of approximately 11.9 million. Conservatively, roughly 20% of those who have suffered a stroke report balance impairment, but individual studies report rates as high as 83% (CDC). Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo is estimated to impact roughly 2.4% of the population over the course of our lifetimes. Among adults over 60, the prevalence rises to about 3.5%, and cumulative lifetime incidence by 80 years old is roughly 10% (Lindell et al., 2024). Conventional rehabilitation programs have persistently faced challenges with patient engagement and adherence (Shahhar et al., 2022). Gamification and VR-based rehabilitation leverage principles of motor learning, neuroplasticity, and intrinsic motivation to address these limitations.

items.title: Human‐Centered Governance: Reconstituting Cognitive Sovereignty in the Age of Algorithmic Systems
items.abstract: Contemporary intelligent systems increasingly participate in shaping, rather than merely supporting, human decision-making processes. While these systems enhance efficiency and predictive performance, they also introduce a critical but underexamined challenge: decisions may remain technically valid while becoming difficult for human actors to interpret and internalize. This misalignment is conceptualized in this study as the meaning gap, defined as the divergence between system output and human interpretive understanding.This paper proposes a human-centered governance framework that positions cognitive sovereignty—the capacity of individuals and institutions to interpret, contextualize, and assume responsibility for decisions—as a necessary condition for sustainable sociotechnical systems. The framework is structured around ten interdependent principles that collectively redefine governance as a cognitive architecture embedded within system design.Drawing on interdisciplinary literature in human–AI interaction, interpretability, and decision science, the study introduces latency as a conceptual construct describing temporal misalignment between system output and human interpretive readiness. This construct provides an integrative lens for understanding phenomena such as delayed comprehension, reduced accountability, and unstable trust in algorithmically mediated environments.Rather than treating interpretability as an auxiliary feature, the proposed framework positions it as a core system function. The paper further outlines potential pathways for operationalizing the meaning gap through measurable indicators, including time-to-comprehension, decision override frequency, and confidence misalignment.While existing frameworks have called for interpretability, few have proposed measurable indicators of cognitive alignment. This paper contributes preliminary metrics—time-to-comprehension, decision override frequency, and confidence misalignment—that operationalize the meaning gap for empirical testing.

items.title: Investigating Ethical Data Communication with Purrsuasion: An Educational Game about Negotiated Data Disclosure
items.abstract: Data communication entails ethical dilemmas where situational constraints forbid full disclosure of source data. Whereas visualization research and pedagogy often frames ethics as a matter of individuals making deceptive design choices or being misled, disclosure problems involve negotiation between pro-social actors. To provide observability into these situated judgments, we contribute Purrsuasion, an open-source visualization game where participants play the roles of (i) data providers designing visualizations subject to disclosure constraints and (ii) data seekers requesting information and awarding a contract. We deploy Purrsuasion in an undergraduate data science class (N = 27), gathering gameplay data to support a mixed-methods analysis of students' communication dynamics, problem solving, and trust formation. We find that difficulties envisioning an ideal visualization solution lead to satisficing in visualization authoring and difficulties attributing authorial intent. Given these challenges, we approach scoring student solutions by developing a heuristic rubric that supports sociotechnical judgments of disclosure adherence.

items.title: Mapping the Challenges of HCI: An Application and Evaluation of ChatGPT for Mining Insights at Scale
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for analytical tasks, yet their effectiveness in real-world applications remains underexamined, partly due to the opacity of proprietary models. We evaluate ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) on the practical task of extracting research challenges from a large scholarly corpus in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). Using a two-step approach, we first apply GPT-3.5 to extract candidate challenges from the 879 papers in the 2023 ACM CHI Conference proceedings, then use GPT-4 to select the most relevant challenges per paper. This process yielded 4,392 research challenges across 113 topics, which we organized through topic modeling and present in an interactive visualization. We compare the identified challenges with previously established HCI grand challenges and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, finding both strong alignment in areas such as ethics and accessibility, and gaps in areas such as human-AI collaboration. A task-specific evaluation with human raters confirmed near-perfect agreement that the extracted statements represent plausible research challenges (κ = 0.97). The two-step approach proved cost-effective at approximately US$50 for the full corpus, suggesting that LLMs offer a practical means for qualitative text analysis at scale, particularly for prototyping research ideas and examining corpora from multiple analytical perspectives.

items.title: Philosophy of Altruism and the Joy of Giving
items.abstract: Altruism, a timeless virtue that transcends cultural boundaries, is the essence of selfless giving and the foundation of genuine human connection. This book by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, explores the intricate relationship between altruistic behavior and the fulfillment of human potential. Published in 2002 by The United Nations and The Education Training Centre, it delves into the ethical and philosophical dimensions of generosity, unraveling how the act of giving contributes to an enriched, more meaningful existence. Through a comprehensive phenomenological approach, this work highlights the profound joy derived from altruism, arguing that the true essence of happiness is deeply rooted in the well-being of others. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, presents a thought-provoking analysis of the intrinsic motivations behind altruism, examining how societies have historically understood and embraced the act of giving. The book was published in 2002 as a response to the growing interest in ethical philosophy, psychological well-being, and global humanitarian efforts. Drawing from a rich tapestry of philosophical traditions and empirical studies, it addresses the fundamental question of whether giving is an obligation, a virtue, or a natural inclination of human beings. Altruism, as defined by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, is an intentional action performed for the benefit of others without expecting a return. This book distinguishes between various forms of altruism, from reciprocal kindness to absolute selflessness. The text further explores how altruism is shaped by social, moral, and psychological frameworks, making it both an individual and collective phenomenon. In an era characterized by increasing individualism, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, investigates why acts of generosity continue to persist. The book presents an exploration of historical and contemporary examples of altruistic behavior, examining how human societies have cultivated cultures of giving. By analyzing these patterns, it uncovers the ways in which altruism influences social cohesion, mental well-being, and ethical consciousness. This book outlines the essential mechanisms through which altruism functions in daily life. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, examines the cognitive and emotional drivers behind selfless acts, demonstrating that the motivation to give stems from a combination of moral philosophy, neurological responses, and socio-cultural conditioning. A critical aspect of this discussion is identifying the markers of altruistic behavior. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, presents a framework for assessing altruism, including psychological traits, behavioral patterns, and societal impact. These indicators provide insight into how selflessness manifests across different contexts. The book investigates variables that influence altruistic tendencies, from genetic predispositions to environmental conditions. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, evaluates how economic status, education, and cultural values shape an individual’s propensity to give, ultimately arguing that altruism is a complex interplay of intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Building on theoretical foundations, this book proposes practical strategies for cultivating altruism at individual and societal levels. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, introduces educational approaches, policy recommendations, and community-driven initiatives that encourage acts of generosity and ethical responsibility. While altruism is celebrated as a moral ideal, it is not without obstacles. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, explores the psychological and societal barriers that hinder the natural inclination to give, such as self-interest, economic limitations, and cultural biases. At the same time, the book highlights key factors that nurture altruistic behavior, including moral education, positive reinforcement, and institutional support. Bringing together the philosophical, ethical, and psychological dimensions of altruism, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, concludes that selflessness is not merely an ethical choice but an essential component of human flourishing. The joy of giving is not only a reflection of compassion but a gateway to enduring happiness and personal growth.

items.title: RoboPlayground: Democratizing Robotic Evaluation through Structured Physical Domains
items.abstract: Evaluation of robotic manipulation systems has largely relied on fixed benchmarks authored by a small number of experts, where task instances, constraints, and success criteria are predefined and difficult to extend. This paradigm limits who can shape evaluation and obscures how policies respond to user-authored variations in task intent, constraints, and notions of success. We argue that evaluating modern manipulation policies requires reframing evaluation as a language-driven process over structured physical domains. We present RoboPlayground, a framework that enables users to author executable manipulation tasks using natural language within a structured physical domain. Natural language instructions are compiled into reproducible task specifications with explicit asset definitions, initialization distributions, and success predicates. Each instruction defines a structured family of related tasks, enabling controlled semantic and behavioral variation while preserving executability and comparability. We instantiate RoboPlayground in a structured block manipulation domain and evaluate it along three axes. A user study shows that the language-driven interface is easier to use and imposes lower cognitive workload than programming-based and code-assist baselines. Evaluating learned policies on language-defined task families reveals generalization failures that are not apparent under fixed benchmark evaluations. Finally, we show that task diversity scales with contributor diversity rather than task count alone, enabling evaluation spaces to grow continuously through crowd-authored contributions. items.title: Safety Mechanisms and Risk Mitigation in Generative AI Mental Health Chatbots: A Systematic Scoping Review
items.abstract: Background: Generative AI (GenAI) mental health chatbots are increasingly being developed to help address persistent barriers to mental healthcare. Unlike earlier rule-based and retrieval-based systems, GenAI chatbots generate open-ended outputs that can be inaccurate and unsafe. Documented harms from general-purpose GenAI chatbots have highlighted the need for purpose-built interventions with dedicated safeguards, yet how safety is implemented in such interventions remains poorly understood. Methods: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, with a prospectively registered and peer-reviewed protocol. A systematic search of seven academic databases and search engines including MEDLINE, Scopus, PsycINFO, ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar and Consensus was conducted in July 2025. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Safety mechanisms and risk mitigation strategies were narratively synthesised across three pre-specified domains: technical safeguards, pre-deployment safety considerations, and delivery-phase risk mitigation strategies. Results: Twenty-one studies across 11 countries were included. Most interventions incorporated at least one technical safety mechanism, most commonly fine-tuning and prompt engineering. A smaller subset implemented layered safety architectures combining retrieval systems, content filters or risk classifiers, and rule-based algorithms. Pre-deployment safeguards included clinical expert and user co-design approaches, research ethics procedures, and data privacy measures. During intervention delivery, detailed onboarding with role clarification was common, but human oversight was limited. Crisis referral protocols varied in rigor but were mostly underdeveloped, and systematic adverse event monitoring was sparse. Documented safety failures included missed suicidal ideation and provision of inaccurate clinical information. Conclusion: GenAI chatbot interventions require a robust sociotechnical approach that integrates technical safeguards with user co-design, procedural controls, and human oversight. Future research is needed to evaluate efficacy, improve safeguards, and standardize safety outcome measurement. Regulatory oversight proportional to the risks these systems carry is required to enable integration into stepped or blended mental healthcare.

items.title: Interoceptive Divergence in Aesthetic Evaluation and Implications for Human-AI Alignment
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), exemplified by large language models (LLMs), is rapidly approaching and in some cases surpassing human performance across a wide range of cognitive tasks. However, human nature is not limited to intelligence alone; it also encompasses sensibility, including the capacity to perceive and experience beauty in visual scenes. This raises a fundamental question: how humans and AI systems converge or diverge in such aesthetic experiences. Aesthetic evaluation depends not only on objective properties of images but also on internal processes within the observer. As part of ongoing efforts in AI alignment, building upon prior human studies that have examined the relationship between beauty ratings, bodily sensations, and emotions, we adopt a comparable set of questionnaire items and present them to LLMs, enabling a direct comparison between human and AI responses. Our comparative analyses revealed that, while humans and AI exhibited broadly similar patterns in the correlations between beauty ratings and emotions, as well as in the image features they prioritized, notable divergences emerged in both the distribution of emotional responses and the relationship between beauty ratings and bodily sensations. These findings suggest that state-of-the-art LLMs, trained on large-scale textual data, can approximate average human tendencies in aesthetic evaluation to a certain extent. However, they also indicate limitations, particularly in relation to interoceptive aspects, which may reflect insufficient representation in training data or unintended consequences of alignment processes. These findings highlight key challenges for AI alignment and suggest important directions for developing AI systems with human-like aesthetic processing.

items.title: Resilient Decentralized Ergodic Coverage for Scalable Multi-Robot Systems in Unknown Time-Varying Environments
items.abstract: Maintaining situational awareness in high-stakes multi-robot applications requires balancing exploration of unobserved regions with sustained monitoring of changing Regions of Interest (ROIs), often under unknown and time-varying distributions, partial observability, and limited communication. We propose a decentralized multi-agent coverage framework that serves as a high-level planning strategy, in which each agent computes an adaptive ergodic policy, implemented via a Markov-chain, that tracks an updated belief over the underlying importance map. Beliefs are maintained online via Gaussian Process (GP) regression from local noisy observations exchanged with neighbors. The resulting policy drives agents to spend time in ROIs in proportion to their estimated importance, while preserving sufficient exploration to detect and adapt to time-varying environmental changes. Unlike existing approaches that assume known importance maps, centralized coordination, or a static environment, our framework addresses the combined challenges of unknown, time-varying distributions under a decentralized, partially observable setting. We further show that our framework is robust to communication and memory degradation, robot loss, and can scale up to hundreds of robots.

items.title: From Self to Others: A Motivational Theory of Intrapersonal and Interpersonal Growth
items.abstract: From Self to Others: A Motivational Theory of Intrapersonal and Interpersonal Growth delves into the intricate relationship between personal motivation and social development. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad presents a compelling theory that connects the drive within an individual to understand and improve themselves (intrapersonal growth) with the equally important journey of building meaningful connections and influence in their social world (interpersonal growth). The book highlights how motivation acts as the essential catalyst bridging self-awareness with empathy, collaboration, and social engagement. This work articulates how nurturing motivation within the self creates pathways to authentic relationships, effective communication, and social harmony. By weaving together psychological insights and practical applications, Rachmad offers a framework that empowers readers to cultivate balanced growth for personal fulfillment and collective wellbeing. Published by UNICEF, this book underscores the universal relevance of harmonizing inner and outer development to foster resilient and compassionate communities. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad authored this book in 1996 as a response to the growing need for a unified understanding of how personal motivation influences social behaviors and vice versa. Recognizing the fragmentation in traditional motivational theories that focused narrowly on individual or social aspects, Rachmad sought to establish a comprehensive theory integrating both domains. The collaboration with UNICEF supported this vision, emphasizing global human development that values both personal insight and interpersonal relations. At its core, this theory distinguishes between intrapersonal growth—the deepening of self-understanding, emotional regulation, and self-motivation—and interpersonal growth—the development of empathy, communication skills, and social connectedness. Motivation is positioned as the dynamic force that activates and sustains growth in both spheres, creating a fluid movement from self-awareness toward meaningful social interaction. This theory emerged from observing how individuals with strong motivational foundations experience enhanced self-esteem and simultaneously engage more positively with others. Conversely, lack of motivation often impairs both self-improvement and social engagement. Societal complexities and rapid interpersonal demands further accentuate the necessity of this integrated motivational perspective. The motivational drive is both intrinsic and relational. Intrinsic motivation fuels personal insight and goal-setting, while relational motivation encourages social bonding and mutual support. These two aspects interact, enabling a cyclical growth pattern that reinforces both self and others’ development. Indicators include sustained self-reflection, purposeful goal pursuit, active listening, empathy in social exchanges, and constructive conflict resolution. Progress in these areas reflects the harmony between intrapersonal and interpersonal motivation. This framework operationalizes variables such as self-motivation intensity, emotional awareness, social engagement frequency, communication quality, and relational satisfaction. Measurement of these variables utilizes psychological scales, behavioral observations, and qualitative assessments. Factors that determine growth include individual personality traits, cultural values, environmental support, educational opportunities, and quality of social relationships. Rachmad stresses the importance of nurturing environments that cultivate both personal ambition and social responsibility. Effective implementation involves educational programs that blend self-awareness exercises with social skills training, community-building activities, mentorship, and reflective practices. UNICEF’s global outreach facilitates the adoption of these strategies in diverse cultural contexts. Challenges include cultural stigmas around expressing inner motivation, social isolation, and educational systems that neglect holistic motivational development. Supportive elements encompass inclusive policies, mental health advocacy, and programs promoting social cohesion. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad concludes that the fusion of intrapersonal and interpersonal motivation is essential for balanced human growth. This theory paves the way for individuals to achieve self-realization while fostering meaningful social contributions, ultimately enhancing collective human potential worldwide. items.title: Head Coil-Mounted Vision Correction Device for Magnetic Resonance Imaging
items.abstract: Correction for nearsightedness and farsightedness is an important concern for functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) experiments involving visual stimuli in humans. In the absence of personal contact lenses, spherical refractive errors are typically corrected using interchangeable lenses mounted in goggles or glasses frames worn by the participant, or mounted on the head coil during scanning. The coil-mounted device described here avoids the ergonomic challenges encountered with head-mounted goggles and addresses limitations of prior coil-mounted designs, including ease of lens switching and inter-pupillary distance adjustments. Our device can be 3D printed economically with MRI-compatible plastics, including PLA.

items.title: Investigating the Impact of Subgraph Social Structure Preference on the Strategic Behavior of Networked Mixed-Motive Learning Agents
items.abstract: Limited work has examined the strategic behaviors of relational networked learning agents under social dilemmas, and has overlooked the intricate social dynamics of complex systems. We address the challenge with Socio-Relational Intrinsic Motivation (SRIM), which endows agents with diverse preferences over sub-graphical social structures in order to study the impact of agents' personal preferences over their sub-graphical relations on their strategic decision-making under sequential social dilemmas. Our results in the Harvest and Cleanup environments demonstrate that preferences over different subgraph structures (degree-, clique-, and critical connection-based) lead to distinct variations in agents' reward gathering and strategic behavior: individual aggressiveness in Harvest and individual contribution effort in Cleanup. Moreover, agents with different subgraphical structural positions consistently exhibit similar strategic behavioral shifts. Our proposed BCI metric captures structural variation within the population, and the relative ordering of BCI across social preferences is consistent in Harvest and Cleanup games for the same topology, suggesting the subgraphical structural impact is robust across environments. These results provide a new lens for examining agents' behavior in social dilemmas and insight for designing effective multi-agent ecosystems composed of heterogeneous social agents.

items.title: The Intellectual Intelligence Catalyst: How Deep Thinking Drives Personal and Professional Breakthroughs
items.abstract: This book explores the profound influence of deep intellectual engagement as the essential catalyst for remarkable personal and professional transformation. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad presents a theory that positions thoughtful reflection, critical analysis, and intentional cognitive effort as the sparks igniting breakthrough achievements. Moving beyond superficial learning, this work highlights how sustained intellectual rigor fosters innovation, problem-solving mastery, and adaptive success in a complex world. Rachmad articulates how nurturing deep thinking not only amplifies intellectual capacity but also serves as a dynamic force empowering individuals to navigate challenges, seize opportunities, and realize their fullest potential. Through practical insights and illustrative cases, readers are guided to embrace the power of concentrated thought as a driver for meaningful change across all life domains. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad wrote this book in 1997 under the auspices of UNICEF, inspired by the emerging recognition that intellectual growth is most potent when rooted in deliberate, focused thinking. The author sought to bridge academic concepts with actionable strategies to help individuals leverage deep cognitive processes for breakthrough development. At the heart of the book lies the definition of deep thinking as reflective, critical, and sustained cognitive engagement that transcends routine knowledge acquisition. Intellectual intelligence, in this context, is the capacity to use such deep thinking to innovate, solve complex problems, and adapt effectively. The theory is grounded in observing how individuals who prioritize and cultivate deep intellectual focus consistently achieve significant advances in both personal and professional spheres. These breakthroughs often stem from moments of insight born from intense cognitive immersion. The catalyst effect occurs as deep thinking activates dormant intellectual resources, strengthens neural pathways, and generates novel perspectives leading to transformative outcomes. Indicators include sustained concentration, critical questioning, integrative reasoning, and the ability to connect disparate ideas meaningfully. Key variables include attention span, reflective capacity, cognitive endurance, motivation to explore complexity, and openness to new information. Essential determinants involve supportive environments that encourage inquiry, availability of time for contemplation, emotional readiness, and access to diverse knowledge sources. The book recommends creating structured time for reflection, fostering curiosity-driven inquiry, encouraging dialectical thinking, and building habits that sustain intellectual rigor. Supportive elements include mentorship, intellectual community, and encouraging feedback. Barriers involve distraction, time pressure, and cultural undervaluing of deep contemplation. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad concludes that deep thinking functions as a powerful catalyst unlocking intellectual intelligence’s transformative potential. By intentionally cultivating this capacity, individuals ignite a process of continuous breakthrough that reshapes their lives and work. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) is an Indonesian scholar, academic leader, and social development advocate with a strong multidisciplinary background. In 2016, YER was awarded the title of Doctor of Humanity, holds a Ph.D. in Information Technology and a DBA in Technology Management. Since 2016, YER has been actively teaching and collaborating with international universities in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and the United States. YER is the founder of the Education Training Centre (ETC, 1992), YER Academic Publishing (YERA, 1993), the Multidisciplinary Academic Institute of Learning (MAIL, 1998), and YER E-Book Publishing (YERE, 1999), institutions dedicated to education, interdisciplinary learning, and ethical academic publishing. His academic contributions have led to his recognition as a Professor and his affiliation with the World Philosophy Foundation. YER is also actively involved in global development initiatives through the United Nations, as a member of the UN Global Compact (id-137635), the UN Global Market (id-709131), and the UN ECOSOC (id-677556). YER has served as a reviewer for several international journals and book chapters, and has written numerous books and articles on a wide range of topics including Philosophy, Economics, Management, The work was inspired by observing how motivation fuels not just academic achievement but lifelong cognitive expansion. The book defines intellectual intelligence as the capacity to acquire, analyze, and utilize knowledge creatively and effectively. Motivation is framed as the energizing force that initiates and sustains this intellectual growth, making the two inseparable components of human development. The author noticed a widespread phenomenon: many individuals possess untapped intellectual abilities due to lack of motivation or inadequate motivational support systems. This inspired the need for a theory that bridges intellectual intelligence with motivational psychology. Intellectual growth thrives in environments where motivation—both internal curiosity and external encouragement—is nurtured. Learning becomes an active, self-directed process fueled by purpose and meaning. Observable markers include persistent curiosity, resilience in facing intellectual challenges, ability to integrate new knowledge, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. These involve motivational drivers (intrinsic interest, goal orientation), cognitive engagement (attention, memory), and environmental factors such as support networks and resources. items.abstract: In a world increasingly shaped by communication and connection, Win Hearts and Minds: Mastering Social Influence with Integrity by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, offers a profound and ethical roadmap to influence. Unlike conventional approaches that often lean toward manipulation, this book is rooted in authenticity and compassion. It invites readers to understand influence not merely as a tool for persuasion, but as a commitment to shared values, trust, and mutual growth. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, draws from years of academic insight, humanitarian service, and leadership experience to craft a thoughtful journey that reveals how hearts and minds can be reached genuinely—without coercion, and with profound respect for human dignity. Published in 1992 in New York by UNICEF, this work remains a timeless guide for leaders, educators, change-makers, and anyone wishing to create meaningful impact through ethical influence. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA wrote Win Hearts and Minds: Mastering Social Influence with Integrity in 1992, in New York, at a time when the global discourse on leadership was shifting toward emotional intelligence and human-centered development. His motivation stemmed from decades of observing both the power and misuse of influence in societal structures. Recognizing the urgent need for a framework rooted in empathy and ethics, he embarked on this work to redefine influence as a vehicle for collective empowerment rather than personal gain. In this publication, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA introduces influence as a multidimensional relationship involving perception, trust, and reciprocal communication. Influence, as framed here, is not a manipulation of others’ decisions but an invitation to co-create shared visions. Concepts such as integrity-based leadership, emotional resonance, and cultural alignment are presented as foundational tools for mastering this dynamic. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA wrote this book in response to the rising phenomena of polarized ideologies, public distrust in leadership, and the erosion of social cohesion. He observed that while technology had made communication easier, authentic connection was diminishing. This book became a response to that global condition, promoting influence not as an imposition but as a means of genuine understanding and social alignment. The guiding principle of this book lies in the alignment between internal values and external actions. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA emphasizes the necessity of consistency, clarity, and compassion in every act of influence. The book outlines how social influence becomes effective when it is transparent, participatory, and purpose-driven. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA outlines indicators of successful influence such as increased stakeholder trust, consistent behavioral alignment, and the presence of shared values. The reader is guided to evaluate the depth of their influence not by popularity or obedience, but by the growth and empowerment of those they influence. Operationally, the book frames influence through several variables defined by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA: relational transparency, cultural empathy, communicative clarity, and ethical congruence. These elements are used to measure both the depth and sustainability of influence in varied contexts. The success of influence, according to Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, is determined by internal integrity, external credibility, situational awareness, and cultural resonance. These factors serve as pillars upon which effective and enduring influence is built. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA discusses implementation through case studies and global examples. Strategic steps include building narrative authenticity, active listening, inclusive dialogue, and ethical decision-making. Influence is portrayed as a living practice, refined continuously through reflection and feedback. In the book, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA acknowledges both the enablers and inhibitors of influence. Challenges include cultural barriers, resistance to change, and miscommunication. Enablers include emotional intelligence, shared purpose, and adaptive leadership. The book emphasizes the importance of resilience and humility in navigating these dynamics. Ultimately, Win Hearts and Minds by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA is a call to lead with humanity. Influence, when exercised with moral clarity and emotional sensitivity, becomes a transformative force. The book closes with the reminder that authentic influence not only changes others—it transforms the influencer.

items.title: AI Disclosure with DAISY
items.abstract: The use of AI tools in research is becoming routine, alongside growing consensus that such use should be transparently disclosed. However, AI disclosure statements remain rare and inconsistent, with policies offering limited guidance and authors facing social, cognitive, and emotional barriers when reporting AI use. To explore how structured disclosure shapes what authors report and how they experience disclosure, we present DAISY (Disclosure of AI-uSe in Your Research), a form-based tool for generating AI disclosure statements. DAISY was developed from literature-derived requirements and co-design (N =11), and deployed in a user study with authors (N=31). DAISY-supported disclosures met more completeness criteria, offering clearer breakdowns of AI use across research and writing than unsupported disclosures. Surprisingly, despite concerns about how transparently disclosed AI use might be perceived, the use of DAISY did not reduce author comfort with the disclosure statements. We discuss design implications and a research agenda for AI disclosure as a sociotechnical practice.

items.title: Celebrity-as-a-Service: Trust and Willingness to Use Digital Twins for Customer Service
items.abstract: A digital twin is an artificial intelligence (AI)- or human-controlled avatar that replicates a specific person’s identity. While organizations have used digital twins of employees (e.g. digital doctors answering patients’ questions), a more common use is celebrity-as-a-service, where digital twins of celebrities interact with customers. Unlike traditional celebrity endorsements in marketing videos, these digital-twin agents interact directly with consumers. Although digital twins do not enhance the underlying AI or human agents’ capabilities, their appearance as a specific person can influence users’ perception. Across two experiments, we found that when a digital twin resembled a celebrity, regardless of whether it was AI- or human-controlled, it was perceived to be more capable, benevolent, and trustworthy, leading to greater user engagement. Even when errors occurred, the celebrity’s likeness reduced negative reactions, suggesting that celebrity effects can buffer against algorithm aversion. Practically, digital celebrity twins offer business value comparable to traditional celebrity endorsements, influencing user trust and service adoption despite identical underlying performance.

items.title: Comparing the Impact of Pedagogy-Informed Custom and General-Purpose GAI Chatbots on Students' Science Problem-Solving Processes and Performance Using Heterogeneous Interaction Network Analysis
items.abstract: Problem solving plays an essential role in science education, and generative AI (GAI) chatbots have emerged as a promising tool for supporting students' science problem solving. However, general-purpose chatbots (e.g., ChatGPT), which often provide direct, ready-made answers, may lead to students' cognitive offloading. Prior research has rarely focused on custom chatbots for facilitating students' science problem solving, nor has it examined how they differently influence problem-solving processes and performance compared to general-purpose chatbots. To address this gap, we developed a pedagogy-informed custom GAI chatbot grounded in the Socratic questioning method, which supports students by prompting them with guiding questions. This study employed a within-subjects counterbalanced design in which 48 secondary school students used both custom and general-purpose chatbot to complete two science problem-solving tasks. 3297 student-chatbot dialogues were collected and analyzed using Heterogeneous Interaction Network Analysis (HINA). The results showed that: (1) students demonstrated significantly higher interaction intensity and cognitive interaction diversity when using custom chatbot than using general-purpose chatbot; (2) students were more likely to follow custom chatbot's guidance to think and reflect, whereas they tended to request general-purpose chatbot to execute specific commands; and (3) no statistically significant difference was observed in students' problem-solving performance evaluated by solution quality between two chatbot conditions. This study provides novel theoretical insights and empirical evidence that custom chatbots are less likely to induce cognitive offloading and instead foster greater cognitive engagement compared to general-purpose chatbots. This study also offers insights into the design and integration of GAI chatbots in science education.

items.abstract: Great Minds Grow: Unlocking the Secrets of Intellectual Development is an insightful exploration into how the human mind can evolve and expand its intellectual capacity. Written by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, and published in 1994 by the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund in New York, USA, this book presents a compelling case for the idea that intellectual growth is not only possible but essential for navigating an increasingly complex world. The book presents key principles, strategies, and practical exercises designed to help readers cultivate their cognitive potential, foster deep thinking, and unlock the secrets to a more intellectually fulfilling life. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, emphasizes that the mind, like a muscle, requires consistent nurturing and engagement to achieve its fullest potential. This book offers a pathway to personal and intellectual growth, showing that the greatest minds are not born but made through dedication and thoughtful practice. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, observed that many individuals were not fully equipped to handle the complex problems and scenarios that emerged in this new era. items.title: Human Thinking under Plural LLM Assistance: Mathematical Problem Solving and Open-Ended Writing
items.abstract: Large language models are changing not only the kind of assistance people receive, but also how that assistance is organized. Instead of working with a single general-purpose chatbot, people can now receive help from systems arranged as peers, specialists, or multiple agents with distinct roles. However, it remains unclear how these forms of plural LLM assistance affect human performance, confidence, and diversity of thought. We conducted two controlled experiments involving 562 participants to examine the effects of using multiple LLMs on mathematical problem-solving and writing. In a math task, participants worked with no LLM, an expert assistant, peer-like agents that surfaced common errors, or both an expert and a peer-like assistant. The expert-plus-peer condition produced the strongest unassisted post-task performance. In a writing task, participants wrote with no LLM, a single generalist assistant, or a pair of role-specialized assistants. LLM assistance improved essay quality, but the role-specialized pair preserved greater idea diversity than the single assistant. Together, these findings identify the arrangement of LLM assistance as a consequential design variable for human-AI collaboration.

items.title: MFE: A Multimodal Hand Exoskeleton with Interactive Force, Pressure and Thermo-haptic Feedback
items.abstract: Recent advancements in virtual reality and robotic teleoperation have greatly increased the variety of haptic information that must be conveyed to users. While existing haptic devices typically provide unimodal feedback to enhance situational awareness, a gap remains in their ability to deliver rich, multimodal sensory feedback encompassing force, pressure, and thermal sensations. To address this limitation, we present the Multimodal Feedback Exoskeleton (MFE), a hand exoskeleton designed to deliver hybrid haptic feedback. The MFE features 20 degrees of freedom for capturing hand pose. For force feedback, it employs an active mechanism capable of generating 3.5-8.1 N of pushing and pulling forces at the fingers' resting pose, enabling realistic interaction with deformable objects. The fingertips are equipped with flat actuators based on the electro-osmotic principle, providing pressure and vibration stimuli and achieving up to 2.47 kPa of contact pressure to render tactile sensations. For thermal feedback, the MFE integrates thermoelectric heat pumps capable of rendering temperatures from 10 to 55 degrees Celsius. We validated the MFE by integrating it into a robotic teleoperation system using the X-Arm 6 and Inspire Hand manipulator. In user studies, participants successfully recognized and manipulated deformable objects and differentiated remote objects with varying temperatures. These results demonstrate that the MFE enhances situational awareness, as well as the usability and transparency of robotic teleoperation systems.

items.title: Social Media and Climate Change: Behavioral Engagement without Deep Cognition? A Systematic Review
items.abstract: This systematic review investigates the relationship between social media use (SMU), climate change cognition (CCC), and pro-environmental intentions (PEI) and behaviors (PEB). The evidence from 21 articles reveals a consistent positive association between SMU and behavioral outcomes (PEI/PEB), whereas its impact on CCC appears fragmented and frequently non-significant. These findings suggest that the social media ecosystem, characterized by informational fragmentation and algorithmic polarization, constrains deep cognitive engagement, instead fostering phenomena such as eco-anxiety and overestimation of knowledge. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), we propose that social media predominantly operates through the peripheral route of persuasion, encouraging immediate yet short-lived behavioral responses driven by social comparison and observational learning rather than critical reflection. In contrast, the literature synthesis supports a set of proposals to activate the central route, thereby enabling sustained and complex pro-environmental behaviors, by leveraging key factors such as intrinsic motivation, digital agency, and exposure to credible scientific sources or strategically designed content, including climate-related memes; absent such conditions, social media is unlikely to produce enduring, cognition-driven environmental behavior change.
